content.text:
**Bun v1.4** is the latest major release (August 20, 2026) of Bun, a fast all-in-one JavaScript and TypeScript runtime, package manager, test runner, and bundler designed as a drop-in replacement for Node.js.[[1]](https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4)

### Major Highlights
- **Rewritten in Rust**: This is the first version where the core (previously in Zig) has been fully rewritten in Rust (~1 million lines of code). The JavaScript engine remains JavaScriptCore (from WebKit), so JS/TS behavior is unchanged, but the surrounding runtime, HTTP server, bundler, package manager, and filesystem layers are now Rust-based. This improves memory safety, compile-time bug detection, and maintainability. The binary is ~20% smaller, and performance matches or exceeds v1.3.[[1]](https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4)
- **Node.js Compatibility**: The biggest jump since v1.0 — **+1,517** passing tests from the Node.js test suite. Many modules (e.g., `node:http`, `node:fs`, `node:cluster`, `node:timers`, `node:zlib`, `node:vm`, `node:stream`, `node:quic`, `node:events`, `node:trace_events`, `node:sqlite`) now pass 97–100% of Node's own tests. This enables better support for frameworks like Next.js 16, Playwright, Vitest, and OpenTelemetry. Over **2,900** GitHub issues were fixed.[[1]](https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4)
- **Performance & Efficiency**:
  - Idle CPU usage reduced by up to **5x**.
  - Memory usage cut by up to **35–48%** (e.g., HTTP servers).
  - Startup ~**50% faster** on Linux (hello-world in ~5.1 ms vs. 10.9 ms in 1.3; Node 26 is ~27 ms) and 2.5x faster on Windows.
  - Significant speedups in many areas: Promises (1.5–2.4x), `new URL()` (4.6x), Markdown parsing (138x in some cases), `Buffer.from()` for hex/base64url (8–46x), source map decoding (3.1x), and `bun:ffi` (up to 3.8x).[[1]](https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4)

### New Built-in APIs (Reducing npm Dependencies)
Bun 1.4 ships a richer standard library to replace many common packages:
- **`Bun.Image`**: Fast image processing (replaces Sharp).
- **`Bun.WebView`**: Headless browser automation (replaces Puppeteer/Playwright). Uses system WebKit on macOS or drives Chrome/Chromium/Edge via CDP on other platforms. Supports navigation, clicks (as trusted input), JS evaluation, screenshots, etc. No extra dependencies needed.[[1]](https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4)
- **`Bun.markdown`**: Native Markdown parsing and rendering (much faster than libraries like Marked).
- **`Bun.cron()`**: Built-in cron job scheduler (replaces node-cron).
- **`Bun.Terminal`**: PTY (pseudo-terminal) support (replaces node-pty).
- Native `ReadableStream`/`WritableStream`/`TransformStream`, `CompressionStream`/`DecompressionStream`.
- `Bun.JSON5` parser.
- Other utilities for TAR archives, parallel script/test running (`bun run --parallel`, `bun test --parallel`), `bun audit fix`, `bun dedupe`, `bun prune`, and more.

This can eliminate 10–15 common npm dependencies in many projects, improving security and reducing supply-chain risks.[[2]](https://www.stork.ai/blog/bun-14-the-update-that-kills-your-dependencies)

### Other Improvements
- **Bundler**: `bun build --compile --target=browser` can now produce a single self-contained HTML file (with JS, CSS, images, etc., inlined). React Compiler is built-in and ~19x faster than via Babel. Better tree-shaking, minification, CSS handling, and source map support.[[3]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=i38DgEuaJwM)
- **HTTP/Server**: Experimental HTTP/2 & HTTP/3 support in `Bun.serve()` and `fetch()`. Improved `Response.clone()`, directory serving, Range/conditional requests.
- **REPL, CLI, and Dev Tools**: Native `bun repl` (with top-level await, better output), Markdown pretty-printing (`bun ./README.md`), parallel testing/running, and more.
- **Windows ARM64** support added.

### Installation & Upgrade
```bash
# Upgrade existing install
bun upgrade

# Fresh install
curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash
```

Official release post: https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4 (highly recommended for full details, benchmarks, and examples).[[1]](https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4)

Overall, Bun 1.4 focuses on production readiness, compatibility, efficiency, and reducing reliance on external packages while maintaining its signature speed. The Rust rewrite generated some community discussion, but the release emphasizes stability (full test suite passing on all platforms with no skipped tests).
